// purpose: debug-generator (apps/vscode-extension) - the EXTENSION HOST compiler project for the monorepo typecheck gate.
// program: What this project covers: everything in this workspace that runs in the VS Code extension host process, which is Node, plus the workspace's build-time and test-time TypeScript (AAP 0.7.1 Group 3). src/extension.ts, src/state.ts, src/uri-handler.ts - activation, the session state held by the host and the `vscode://debuggen.debug-generator/open` handler with its own containment validation (AAP 0.2.3). src/service/** - the reconnecting client, the embedded-service process manager, workspace/dev-server discovery and the $DEBUGGEN_HOME/auth.json reader. src/commands/** - the twelve contributed commands of package.json. src/views/** - the webview view provider and the Sessions tree. src/source/** - showTextDocument with a selection range. src/webview-messages.ts - the typed host<->webview message union (see the deliberate overlap note under `exclude`). test/** - the @vscode/test-cli suites run by `pnpm test:vscode`. vite.config.ts - the webview bundle's build config.
// two-projects: What this project deliberately does NOT cover: src/webview/**. That React application is a page, not a Node process, and it is the exclusive program of the SECOND project in this directory, tsconfig.webview.json. The split is the whole point of having two projects here - it keeps DOM globals out of the host (see `lib`) and Node globals out of the browser bundle - and both projects are named by `pnpm --filter debug-generator typecheck` (`tsc -b tsconfig.json tsconfig.webview.json`) and both are listed in the root solution file's `references`, as the entries `apps/vscode-extension` and `apps/vscode-extension/tsconfig.webview.json`. Until this workspace's first source file lands, an input-less project answers `tsc -b` with TS18003 ("No inputs were found in config file"), and because both projects are already named by the root solution file that error is what the repository-wide gate reports at this boundary: running `tsc -b` on this file today reports exactly that for this project, for the webview project and for the referenced packages whose src/** has not landed yet - expected on an empty subtree, not a configuration fault.
// not-a-build: This project does NOT build the extension either. dist/ is written exclusively by esbuild.mjs (the CommonJS host bundle at dist/extension.js, the embedded service at dist/service/main.js and the telemetry preload) and by `vite build` (dist/webview/**); this project emits declarations only, into .tsbuild/ (see `outDir`). typescript-eslint's project service reads this same file for the type information behind the type-aware rules, which is why test/** and vite.config.ts are inside `include` rather than only src/**.
// inherited: Everything not stated below is inherited from tsconfig.base.json and must stay that way - in particular `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `isolatedModules`, `moduleDetection: "force"`, `noImplicitOverride`, `noImplicitReturns`, `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`, `noUnusedLocals`, `noUnusedParameters`, `forceConsistentCasingInFileNames`, `target` ES2023, `allowJs: false` and `skipLibCheck` (the base's decision about third-party .d.ts drift, neither widened nor restated here). No strictness flag is relaxed, no `any`-friendly flag is added, and no compiler or compiler package is declared: TypeScript 6.0.3 is pinned once, in the root manifest (AAP 0.3.1), so no 7.x-only option appears here. `noEmit` must never be added: TypeScript 6.0.3 rejects a referenced project that disables emit with TS6310 and the whole gate fails.
// format: Strict JSON, like the root tsconfig.json, tsconfig.base.json and every other tsconfig in this repository: both a JSONC-aware reader (`ts.readConfigFile`) and a bare `JSON.parse` read it, so no consumer - tsc, typescript-eslint's project service, Vitest, Vite or Prettier - has to know which one to reach for. The rationale therefore lives in the `"// …"` string keys of this object rather than in comments. TypeScript ignores unknown TOP-LEVEL keys, which is what makes the convention safe; a `"// …"` key inside `compilerOptions` is a hard error instead (TS5023, "Unknown compiler option"), so every note about a single option lives up here under a `"// compilerOptions.<option>"` key and never beside the option itself.
// compilerOptions.composite: Already true in the base; restated because the root solution file references this project and a non-composite reference fails `tsc -b` outright (TS6306). Keeping it local means a future edit to the base cannot silently break the gate at this project. esbuild and Vite do not read this option - both transpile per file - so its value serves the gate alone.
// compilerOptions.rootDir: "." and not "src", because this program deliberately spans three input roots: src/**, test/** and vite.config.ts (see `include`), whose common root is the workspace directory. `rootDir: "src"` would reject the other two with TS6059 ("is not under 'rootDir'"), and leaving it unset would let the compiler infer a root from the longest common prefix - which changes whenever a file is added or removed, moving the whole declaration tree with it. Pinned here, the mirror under .tsbuild/ is stable: src/extension.ts -> .tsbuild/src/extension.d.ts, test/suite/uri-handler.test.ts -> .tsbuild/test/suite/uri-handler.d.ts and vite.config.ts -> .tsbuild/vite.config.d.ts. apps/local-service pins it the same way for the same reason (its integration suite also lives outside src/).
// compilerOptions.declaration: `declaration`, `declarationMap` and `emitDeclarationOnly` are inherited true from the base and restated so the "declarations, never JavaScript" guarantee is local to this project: `composite` forbids `noEmit` (TS6310), so emitting nothing but .d.ts/.d.ts.map is the only shape that satisfies both the gate and the bundlers' ownership of dist/.
// compilerOptions.outDir: Declaration-only emit, restated with the `${configDir}` anchoring the base uses (apps/chrome-extension and apps/demo-app restate it the same way). `${configDir}` resolves to the directory of THIS file, so every artefact of the typecheck gate lands in apps/vscode-extension/.tsbuild - ignored by .gitignore, by .prettierignore and by the `**/.tsbuild/**` entry in eslint.config.js, so the gate never shows up in `git status`. A repository-level path such as ../../.tsbuild/vscode-extension would sit outside the per-workspace convention every sibling follows and outside those three ignore lists. What must never happen: tsc writing into apps/vscode-extension/dist. That directory belongs to esbuild.mjs and `vite build` byte for byte - it is what package.json's `main` points at, what `.vscodeignore` keeps in the VSIX, and what the packaged-VSIX smoke test installs - so a stray .d.ts or .js from the gate in there would be shipped inside the extension.
// compilerOptions.tsBuildInfoFile: The output directory and the stamp are the base's own values, kept because THIS is the workspace's first project: the base reserves the override for the SECOND project in the same directory, so tsconfig.webview.json is what moves its output and its stamp into .tsbuild/webview/. Two projects sharing one output directory overwrite each other's declarations and two projects sharing one .tsbuildinfo never settle, so the pair of paths here and the pair there must stay distinct.
// compilerOptions.lib: The base's ES2023-only set, restated so the boundary against tsconfig.webview.json is local and explicit rather than inherited: this program is the extension HOST, a Node 24 process with no document. A host file that reaches for `window`, `document`, `localStorage` or DOM's `WebSocket`/`MessageEvent` must fail to compile, because at runtime it would throw - the host talks to the webview through the typed messages of src/webview-messages.ts and `webview.postMessage`, and to the local service through `ws` 8.21.3 (a Node socket, typed by @types/ws), never through a browser global. The webview project is the only place in this workspace where "DOM" and "DOM.Iterable" are legitimate, and it declares them itself. ES2023 must be spelled out in full whenever `lib` appears at all, because `lib` REPLACES the inherited array rather than merging with it; the single entry here is therefore the same value the base sets, not a narrowing.
// compilerOptions.types: The base sets no `types`, so one workspace's ambient globals cannot bleed into another. This project needs exactly two - "node", "vscode" - and nothing else; the two notes below say why each one is there, and the `not-listed` notes say why the obvious candidates are absent.
// compilerOptions.types.vscode: @types/vscode 1.125.0, a devDependency of this workspace and the reason `import * as vscode from "vscode"` resolves at all: the package is one big `declare module "vscode"`, an ambient module declaration that must be a program member. It types every API the host uses - `window.registerWebviewViewProvider`, `window.registerUriHandler`, `window.showTextDocument` with a selection, `commands.registerCommand`, `workspace.workspaceFolders`, `ExtensionContext.extensionUri` - and it must stay pinned to the same 1.125.0 that package.json's `engines.vscode` declares, so the compiler cannot offer an API the minimum supported editor lacks. At runtime the module is supplied by the editor, which is why esbuild.mjs marks it external.
// compilerOptions.types.node: @types/node 24.13.6, a ROOT devDependency resolved by walking up to the workspace-root node_modules/@types. Do NOT add it to this workspace's manifest. The host is a Node process: `node:fs`/`node:path`/`node:os` for $DEBUGGEN_HOME and auth.json, `node:child_process` for spawning the embedded service and the dev server, `process.env` for the environment it passes them, plus the globals @types/ws and the test suites build on. vite.config.ts uses `node:path`/`node:url` for the same reason.
// compilerOptions.types.not-listed.moch: Not listed: "mocha", and no @types/mocha entry exists in package.json - the dependency inventory AAP 0.3.2 freezes for this workspace does not include one, and @vscode/test-cli 0.0.15 keeps its own copy of @types/mocha inside the virtual store, where a `types` entry cannot reach it, so naming it here would be an unresolvable entry (TS2688). The extension-host suites under test/suite/** run in a real editor under @vscode/test-cli, whose runner is Mocha, so `describe`, `it`, `before`, `after`, `beforeEach` and `afterEach` are AMBIENT GLOBALS there - the one place in the repository where a test does not import its harness - and the suites declare the ones they use in an ambient declaration file of their own under test/, which is a program member through the `include` below and needs no @types package. That is the single mechanism for those globals: putting "mocha" back alongside it would declare them twice (TS2300). Every Vitest suite in every other workspace imports `{ describe, it, expect }` from "vitest" explicitly, and the webview suites collected by the `vscode-extension-webview` Vitest project do the same inside the OTHER project, which is why "vitest/globals" appears in neither.
// compilerOptions.types.not-listed: Not listed: "react" / "react-dom". They are not ambient global type packages, and no .tsx file is a member of this project anyway - the React application is tsconfig.webview.json's program. Not listed: "chrome" - the MV3 surfaces live in apps/chrome-extension.
// compilerOptions.module: NOT overridden: "module" / "moduleResolution", and this is a correctness requirement rather than a style choice. The base's "ESNext" + "bundler" is the flavour AAP 0.3.4 assigns to extension code, and it is what lets this workspace author ESM and consume the ESM-only `@debuggen/*` packages while SHIPPING CommonJS: package.json declares no `"type": "module"`, because VS Code loads `main: dist/extension.js` as CJS. Switch this project to NodeNext and every file here becomes a CommonJS module, so - with `verbatimModuleSyntax` inherited from the base - the `import`/`export` syntax itself stops compiling (TS1295 "ECMAScript imports and exports cannot be written in a CommonJS file under 'verbatimModuleSyntax'" and TS1287), and a file rewritten to `require()` would then reject the ESM-only "." export of @debuggen/protocol on its own (TS1479). Verified both ways against TypeScript 6.0.3 with a CJS consumer and an ESM-only dependency. Authoring ESM and letting esbuild.mjs emit the CJS bundle is the deliberate design; bundler resolution is what type-checks it.
// compilerOptions.module.specifiers: CONVENTION FOR EVERY FILE IN src/** AND test/**: relative specifiers are EXTENSIONLESS - `import { ServiceClient } from "./service/client";` and `import type { HostToWebviewMessage } from "../webview-messages";` - as in apps/chrome-extension and packages/panel-renderer, and the exact opposite of the ".js"-suffixed convention that packages/shared, packages/protocol, packages/telemetry and apps/local-service must use because they override this setting to NodeNext. The compiler will not catch a specifier copied from one of those: bundler resolution applies the same TypeScript extension substitution, so "./client.js" also resolves to client.ts here (confirmed with tsc 6.0.3). Consistency is therefore a review matter - write no extension. The reverse mistake IS a compile error: an extensionless relative import that reports TS2835 ("did you mean './x.js'?") means this setting was overridden to NodeNext by accident, and the config is what gets fixed, never the imports. Package specifiers carry no extension in either flavour ("vscode", "ws", "@debuggen/protocol") and resolve through the pnpm workspace symlink and each package's `exports` map.
// compilerOptions.module.top-level-awai: Also relevant to authoring, because the compiler cannot catch it: esbuild cannot lower top-level `await` into a CommonJS bundle, so host modules must keep their awaits inside functions - `activate()` is `async` and everything asynchronous hangs off it.
// compilerOptions.jsx: NOT overridden: "jsx". The base's "react-jsx" is inert here because no .tsx file is a program member; the webview project is where it matters.
// compilerOptions.not-set: NOT set: "paths" / "baseUrl". The three workspace dependencies resolve through their `exports` maps plus the project references below, exactly as the runtime and esbuild resolve them (AAP 0.2.2) - esbuild.mjs depends on that being true, and an alias to a sibling's src/** would hide a broken `exports` map and let the acyclic package layering be violated without anything failing. Because those maps point at each package's dist/index.d.ts, which lies outside the `${configDir}/.tsbuild` declaration directory, no output-to-source redirect applies to that target. Each package's `types` condition is therefore a fallback array, dist/ first and src/ second: a built tree resolves the dist/ declarations exactly as the bundlers ship them, while a tree with no dist/ yet (a fresh clone) resolves the source entry, which `tsc -b` redirects to that referenced project's own `.tsbuild` declarations. That is what lets `pnpm typecheck` stand alone without `pnpm build` (AAP 0.8.5), and tests/e2e/clean-clone.spec.ts proves it on a fresh copy of the tree.
// include: The host program, in three parts. "src/**/*.ts" - every host module listed under `"// program"`. No .tsx glob: this project compiles no JSX, and src/webview/** is excluded below. "test/**/*.ts" - the @vscode/test-cli suites (activation, commands, open-location, uri-handler, packaged-vsix per AAP 0.7.1 Group 3). They are deliberately program members so the gate type-checks them: `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noUnusedLocals` and `noUnusedParameters` apply to tests exactly as to sources, and an untypechecked test is how contract drift escapes. They are NOT a Vitest project, because these suites need a real extension host where the `vscode` module exists. The root vitest.config.ts collects two other trees of this workspace instead: src/webview/** (`vscode-extension-webview`, happy-dom) and host logic colocated as src/**/*.test.ts outside src/webview/** (`vscode-extension-host`, Node, with the `vscode` module substituted through `vi.mock`); those colocated host suites are members of this project through "src/**/*.ts" and are type-checked here. "vite.config.ts" - the webview bundle's build config. It is a TypeScript file, so it must belong to a project or the type-aware `pnpm lint` gate rejects it as "not included in any project"; `vite` 8.3.0 is a root devDependency and its types resolve through pnpm's parent-directory walk. A literal path that does not exist yet contributes nothing to the program (only a `files` entry would error), so this stays correct while the workspace is being built out. Nothing else: esbuild.mjs and .vscode-test.mjs are plain Node ESM, linted but never compiled (`allowJs: false`), and media/** holds only the icons.
// exclude: Replaces the base's inherited list rather than merging with it, so the output and vendored directories are named again here; every entry is resolved relative to this directory.
// exclude.src-webview: "src/webview/**" is the load-bearing entry and the reason this workspace has two projects: those React sources are claimed exclusively by tsconfig.webview.json, and two composite projects must not both compile them - the duplicate program would type-check the same files twice with different `lib`/`types` and emit two declaration trees for one module.
// exclude.webview-messages: DELIBERATE EXCEPTION, which must be preserved: src/webview-messages.ts stays INSIDE this project (matched by "src/**/*.ts" and not excluded) while tsconfig.webview.json includes it too. A relative import cannot cross a composite project boundary and both halves of the workspace import that module, so the overlap is the only way to type one message union for both sides. It is safe precisely because the module is type-only - types, the discriminated-union message shapes and const maps, no runtime side effects - and because the two projects emit into separate .tsbuild/ subdirectories. Do not "fix" it by relocating the file, by duplicating the types (a second definition of a cross-boundary shape is the defect AAP 0.2.3 forbids) or by adding a third project.
// exclude.test-fixtures: "test/fixtures/**" follows the convention of apps/local-service, packages/instrumentation and packages/code-analysis: a fixture tree is a runtime input the suites copy, open or index, not a program file, and compiling one would drag a foreign project's sources into this program. The corollary those three workspaces also follow, and the reason this is written down: a fixture tree carries its OWN tsconfig.json (as packages/instrumentation/test/fixtures/project-a does), because under `parserOptions.projectService` in eslint.config.js a .ts file that no project claims is a parsing error rather than a lint finding. Verified with the project service against this file: src/**, test/** and vite.config.ts resolve to this project, and src/webview/** resolves to tsconfig.webview.json.
// exclude.outputs: ".vscode-test" is where @vscode/test-electron unpacks a full VS Code build (or is symlinked to the shared /opt/vscode-test-cache); "dist" belongs to esbuild and Vite; ".tsbuild" is this project's own declaration output, and it is repeated from the base because TypeScript excludes `outDir` automatically only when `exclude` is absent - without it the emitted declarations, including the webview project's under .tsbuild/webview/, would become inputs of the next run.
// exclude.scope: Note what `exclude` does NOT do: it filters the `include` globs only, so a file reached by an import still joins the program - `rootDir` above is what keeps inputs inside this workspace.
// references: Exactly two, foundational-first to match the root solution's ordering, and exactly the `@debuggen/*` edges the HOST half of this workspace has. ../../packages/shared - ids, `Result`, the POSIX project-relative path normalisation and containment check the URI handler and the source-open command validate with, the error types and the logger, plus the single `SourceLocation` schema every located runtime item carries (AAP 0.2.3). ../../packages/protocol - the message envelope and every WS/HTTP schema, `SessionRecord`, `AnalysisResult` and the reconnecting client SDK src/service/client.ts drives. Both extensions import this and never service internals (AAP 0.4.2).
// references.not-referenced: NOT referenced, each for its own reason. packages/panel-renderer - a dependency of the WORKSPACE, imported only by src/webview/** for tokens and primitives, so the reference belongs in tsconfig.webview.json; host code has no page to render into. apps/local-service - even though esbuild.mjs bundles its sources into dist/service/main.js so the VSIX is self-contained: that bundling happens outside the type system, and a project reference would make an editor extension a compile-time dependent of the service and create an edge the AAP's layering forbids. The service is reached over HTTP and WebSocket, and its contract is @debuggen/protocol. apps/chrome-extension and apps/demo-app - sibling processes and an instrumentation target; a reference or import would additionally fail `pnpm check:no-hardcoding` (AAP 0.5.4).
// references.effect: What the references do, precisely: they order the build, so `tsc -b` on this project (or on the root solution) builds packages/shared, then packages/protocol - and, through protocol's own references, packages/telemetry, packages/instrumentation and packages/panel-schema - before this project, and reports errors in dependency order. They are not what resolves the two specifiers; the `exports` maps are, per the `"// compilerOptions.not-set"` note above.
